text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English-born American inventor ELIHU THOMSON was born in 1835. He was co-founder of the General-Electric company with THOMAS EDISON.
British architect EDWIN LUTYENS was born in 1869 . He was famous for his work on the vice-regal palace in NEW DELHI.
British composer WILLIAM WALTON was born in 1902. He was best known for his composition 'Facade'.
U.S. comedian BOB HOPE was born in 1903.
Australian politician and champion cyclist Sir HUBERT OPPERMAN, who was known as "Oppy", was born in 1904.
American jazz singer PEARL BAILEY was born in 1918. She was best known for her role in the all-black version of 'Hello Dolly".

British singer GARY BROOKER was born in 1945. His first hit was 'Poison Ivy' in 1963. He later recorded a series of songs with a group of musician friends, who didn't intend forming a band. That changed in 1967 after their one of their songs became one of the biggest hits of all time. The group was 'Procol Harum', and the song was "Whiter Shade of Pale."
Rock musican FRANCIS ROSSI was born in 1950. He gained fame as the lead singer of 'Status Quo'.
** EVENTS **
1827 : 10,000 people went to the funeral of composer
LUDWIG VAN BEETHOVEN in Vienna. The great composer was best known for his symphonies, in particular his 5th and 9th. During the last 20 years of his life he suffered extreme deafness.
1871 : QUEEN VICTORIA opens the Royal Albert Hall in
London.
1886 : COCA-COLA went on sale for the first time. The
first bottles were sold at the pharmacy in Atlanta Georgia, where it was marketed as a health drink by its inventor Dr JOHN PEMBERTON.
1891 : British explorer ROBERT SCOTT dies after reaching
the South Pole.
1921 : After years of argument and many arrests,
Britain's suffragettes won their battle for the vote. The British Parliament gave the vote to all women over the age of 21.
1947 : Miss MABEL HOWARD became the first woman member of
Cabinet in New Zealand.
1957 : Irish-born writer JOYCE CAREY died.
1973 : U.S. troops began pulling out of Vietnam.
1979 : Ugandan dictator IDI AMIN went into hiding in the
interior of his country after his government was toppled by forces from neighbouring Tanzania.
1989 : French President FRANCOIS MITTERAND inaugrated a
vast glass pyramid in front of the Louvre museum in Paris. The residents of the city hated it, and demanded it be torn down.
1989 : Soviet Communists went to the polls in the first
multi-party elections since 1917 and suffered big losses. While the elections for Congress set them back, they stayed in power. The winners were candidates backed by Russian President BORIS YELTSIN.
1994 : Former president of the German Democratic
Republic, ERICH HONECKER, died of liver cancer at the age of 81.
